content: During the day, sunlight travels through a long path of the atmosphere, causing most of the shorter blue wavelengths to scatter away from your eyes while the longer red and yellow wavelengths pass through directly. However, at sunset, the sun is lower in the sky, so its light must travel through a much longer path through the atmosphere. This extended journey allows even the red and orange wavelengths to scatter away, leaving only the red and orange hues to reach your eyes.
